subject: zoology
question_text: What is cyclomorphosis? Explain its importance in Daphnia.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.60, VSAQ 153). page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: Cyclomorphosis is the cyclic seasonal change
in the body shape of an organism.
steps.why: The word has two halves — cyclo for the cycle and morphosis for the change of shape — and the definition must carry both, because a seasonal change that does not come back is not cyclomorphosis.
common_mistakes: Writing that the animal changes colour. Cyclomorphosis is a change of SHAPE.
Leaving out the word seasonal. The change follows the seasons and returns each year.
steps.memory_tip: Cyclo = the cycle comes round again, morphosis = the shape changes.
steps.margin_note: One sentence with the words cyclic and seasonal, then the example.

steps.label: Importance in Daphnia

lines.text: The hood of Daphnia grows and shrinks

lines: The hood is an adaptation to the changing
Spring: a hood starts to grow.
Summer: a large hood is formed.
Autumn: the hood begins to shrink, and by
winter the head is round again.
steps.why: The four seasons in order show the cycle closing, which is the point of the word cyclomorphosis; a list without the return to the round head does not show a cycle.
common_mistakes: Describing only the summer hood. The mark is for the full round of seasons.
Writing that the hood is for swimming faster. It answers the changing DENSITY of the water.
steps.memory_tip: Round, growing, largest, shrinking — winter, spring, summer, autumn, then round again.
steps.margin_note: The four seasons in order, one short line each. End back at the round head.

insider_note: The season list is what earns the second mark, and it must close the loop — a student who stops at the summer hood has not shown a cycle.
